text: Twenty seven drops of same size are charged at 220 V each. They combine to form a bigger drop. Calculate the potential of the bigger drop.
solution:
Electric potential due to a charged sphere \(= \dfrac{kQ}{R}\)
\(k = 9\times10^9\) N-m\(^2\)/C\(^2\)
\(Q\): charge on sphere
\(R\): Radius of sphere
Let charge and radius of smaller drop is \(q\) and \(r\) respectively
For smaller drop, \(V = \dfrac{kq}{r} = 220\) V
Let \(R\) be radius of bigger drop,
As volume remains the same
\(\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\right)\times27 = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3\)
\(\Rightarrow R = \sqrt[3]{27}\ r = 3r\)
Now, using charge conservation,
\(\Rightarrow Q = 27q\)
\(V_{big\ drop} = \dfrac{kQ}{R} = \dfrac{k(27q)}{3r} = 9\left(\dfrac{kq}{r}\right)\)
\(= 9\times220 = 1980\) V

text: Compound P (C\(_8\)H\(_8\)O) gives a red orange precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent and it does not reduce Fehling's reagent. On drastic oxidation with chromic acid, P gives an aromatic product Q that produces effervescence on treating with aq. NaHCO\(_3\). Compounds P and Q, respectively, are :
solution:
Degree of unsaturation (= (8+1) - dfrac{8}{2} = 5): a benzene ring (4) and one C=O.
A red orange precipitate with 2,4-DNP shows an aldehyde or a ketone.
No reduction of Fehling's reagent: P is a ketone, or an aromatic aldehyde, since aromatic aldehydes do not respond to Fehling's test.
If P is acetophenone, (	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_5	ext{COCH}_3), drastic oxidation with chromic acid gives benzoic acid, Q, which gives (	ext{CO}_2) with (	ext{NaHCO}_3): option (D).
If P is 4-methylbenzaldehyde, p-(	ext{CH}_3	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_4	ext{CHO}), drastic oxidation turns both the CHO and the (	ext{CH}_3) group into COOH, giving terephthalic acid, which also gives (	ext{CO}_2) with (	ext{NaHCO}_3): option (C).
So both (C) and (D) fit the data, and the official key accepts (C) or (D).

text:
The reagent 'R' in the given sequence of chemical reaction is:
\[\text{2,4,6-tribromoaniline} \xrightarrow[0\text{-}5^\circ\text{C}]{NaNO_2, \; HCl} \text{2,4,6-tribromobenzenediazonium chloride} \xrightarrow{R} \text{1,3,5-tribromobenzene}\]
solution: 2,4,6-tribromoaniline \(\xrightarrow[0-5^\circ\text{C}]{NaNO_2, HCl}\) 2,4,6-tribromobenzenediazonium chloride \(\xrightarrow[(R)]{CH_3CH_2OH}\) 1,3,5-tribromobenzene. Reagent R is \(C_2H_5OH\) with diazonium salt.
